hyunjun_ch1.001: You take the stairs slowly. Not on purpose. He stops on every step as if each one were a station.

hyunjun_ch1.025: Yes. Sit. We have time. We have more time than I know what to do with.

hyunjun_ch1.066: Three. The roof. No reason. That's the reason.
hyunjun_ch1.067: If there is room on your line, I would like to request a stop.

hyunjun_ch1.070: By the owner. Four years ago. I will explain at the stop. It is not bad. It is, I believe, only embarrassing.

hyunjun_ch1.075: I don't know what it is yet. Usually that's where I'd write six things, so it wasn't empty.

hyunjun_ch1.081: Take the pen. "You're trusting me with the front desk's property."
hyunjun_ch1.082: It's a shared crime now. If they ask, we were together the whole time. Which is true. That's the best kind of alibi.
hyunjun_ch1.083: Take the pen, and keep hold of the receipt's other corner a second longer.
hyunjun_ch1.084: For a moment you're both holding the same thin strip of paper, one thumb each. It would tear if either of you pulled. Neither of you pulls.
hyunjun_ch1.085: ...It's a good map. I can tell already. It has the right people on it.
hyunjun_ch1.086: He folds the receipt once, along the line, and puts it in the chest pocket of the bomber. Then he takes it out to check it's still a map. It is.
hyunjun_ch1.087: An hour forty-seven, five stops. Twenty minutes each, near enough. That's generous.
hyunjun_ch1.088: We can walk. At an ordinary pace. Come on. Stop one. He's had that bag for over two hours, and he's fast.

hyunjun_ch2.102: I came to rescue the bag.

hyunjun_ch3.001: The practice room smells of floor polish and old speakers. Somebody left the lights on the lowest setting.
hyunjun_ch3.002: One wall is mirror, floor to ceiling. No tunnel behind it. No train attached. Just the room again, and the two of you in it.
hyunjun_ch3.003: Hyunjun walks a lap of it before he says anything. You've stopped expecting otherwise.
hyunjun_ch3.004: So. The thing I can't do.
hyunjun_ch3.005: You know at the end of a song? The music stops, and you hold the last pose. Eight counts. Breathing hard. The camera stays on you.
hyunjun_ch3.006: People love that part. It's the part where you get to look at someone who just finished something.
hyunjun_ch3.008: And I walk off on five.

hyunjun_ch3.019: Walk to where he stopped, and look at the mark his shoe left on the floor.
hyunjun_ch3.020: A grey scuff, fresh, at the end of a line of older scuffs. All the same length. All pointing at the door.

hyunjun_ending_beside.025: You go up alone. You come down with a box.
hyunjun_ending_beside.026: It's not heavy. The tape on it is three flats old: brown, then clear over the brown, then a strip of blue from somewhere you'd forgotten.
hyunjun_ending_beside.027: You put it on the front step. Hyunjun stays on the pavement, exactly where he said he would, and opens the paper bag.
hyunjun_ending_beside.028: Scissors. Two thousand five hundred won. I said I'd hold the scissors. I didn't have any. It was bothering me.
hyunjun_ending_beside.029: He hands them over, handles first, and then turns to look, with great interest, at a parked scooter.
hyunjun_ending_beside.032: I'm asking you to. That's what I want the person by the door for.
hyunjun_ending_beside.033: He turns round. He comes and sits on the step, on the other side of the box, and waits.
hyunjun_ending_beside.034: The blue tape goes first. Then the clear. Then the brown.
hyunjun_ending_beside.035: Inside, there is a shoebox, and inside the shoebox there are transit cards.
hyunjun_ending_beside.036: A dozen of them. More. Every city you ever lived in, each in its own colours, held together with a hair elastic that's gone slack.
hyunjun_ending_beside.038: They've all got money on. A little. One ride, maybe two.
hyunjun_ending_beside.039: I never ran one down to zero. If I did, I was finished with the place.
hyunjun_ending_beside.040: He picks up the top one and turns it over, carefully, the way he handled the glass card.
hyunjun_ending_beside.041: One more stop. On every one of them.
hyunjun_ending_beside.042: You've been doing it too. The whole time. You just did it quietly, in a shoebox, and I did it out loud in restaurants.
hyunjun_ending_beside.043: You hadn't known that was what the box was. Now it's open, it seems the only thing it could have been.
hyunjun_ending_beside.044: He unclips the card from his own lanyard, the one with the fox charm, and holds it next to yours. Same city. Same green.
hyunjun_ending_beside.045: This one you run down. All the way. Then you top it up, and run it down again. That's what staying is. It's really boring. It's just topping up a card.
hyunjun_ending_beside.047: It's not. I'll remind you. That's my job now.
hyunjun_ending_beside.048: Can I say the real thing? I worked it out on the bridge.
hyunjun_ending_beside.049: I want to be your first number. The one you ring. Flat tyre, bad day, new ice cream, can't find the good exit at a station.
hyunjun_ending_beside.050: And you're mine. You already are. You were the vote all night. I'm just making it official.
hyunjun_ending_beside.051: It's not instead of anything. It's not the small version. It's the thing. I've got seven people I'd walk across the city for. Now I've got eight.
hyunjun_ending_beside.052: You have had a phone for years. The line that says who to call has always been blank, because you were never anywhere long enough to fill it in.
hyunjun_ending_beside.053: You fill it in on the step. He watches you type his name, and corrects the spelling of his own nickname for himself, which is *Inside Lane*.
hyunjun_ending_beside.055: I gave you the inside lane in the hallway at two a.m. You don't remember. It was a significant gesture.
hyunjun_ending_beside.056: He stands up. Brushes off his knees.
hyunjun_ending_beside.057: Right. I'm going home. I can, because it's not the end of anything.
hyunjun_ending_beside.058: Saturday. I'm bringing all seven. We're doing the rest of your boxes. Songha's going to make a schedule for your kitchen, and you're going to let him.
hyunjun_ending_beside.061: He goes. Down the street, past the scooter, toward the bridge. He doesn't ask for one more of anything.
hyunjun_ending_beside.062: At the corner he turns round and walks four steps backwards, smiling, to check you're still on the step. You are.

hyunjun_ending_someday.002: He gets there. You watch him get there. It goes across his face like the lights of a station through a window.

hyunjun_ending_someday.013: I'm choosing my words. It happens. Mark the date.
hyunjun_ending_someday.014: He takes the card in both hands. The river shows through it. He looks at the picture, and then over the top of it, at you, and doesn't hurry back to the picture.
hyunjun_ending_someday.015: Hapjeong, before the first train. The platform is so clean and empty it looks like it's been set out for someone.
hyunjun_ending_someday.016: The board says three minutes. Your stop is one past the river. His is a ten-minute walk the other way, and he has come down here anyway, and said so.
hyunjun_ending_someday.017: I'm not getting on. I want that on record. I walked you to a train and I'm not getting on it. Personal best.
hyunjun_ending_someday.018: He's holding the pole by the yellow line with one hand. Not bracing, this time. Just holding it, the way you'd hold a railing on a balcony.
hyunjun_ending_someday.019: I'm going to say it, though. Here. Out loud. I'm not mailing this one to myself.
hyunjun_ending_someday.020: I like you. Not the nickname kind. The other kind. The kind where I go into a shop and come out with one thing, and it's yours.
hyunjun_ending_someday.021: I think I have since about Dangsan. Four years ago. I just didn't have anywhere to put it.
hyunjun_ending_someday.022: "I like you too. The other kind."
hyunjun_ending_someday.023: It's easy. You'd thought it would be a bigger sentence. It's the same size as *hi, bridge*.
hyunjun_ending_someday.024: "I counted the stops after Sindorim. All the way home. That's when it was, for me."
hyunjun_ending_someday.025: You say it to the yellow line, and then, because he said his out loud, you look up and say the rest: *I like you too.*
hyunjun_ending_someday.027: Good. Both of us. At the same time. That almost never lines up.
hyunjun_ending_someday.028: He lets go of the pole and takes one step closer. Just the one. He leaves the rest of the distance to you.
hyunjun_ending_someday.029: Here's the thing. I know me. If we start right now, I'll do fourteen stops of it by lunchtime.
hyunjun_ending_someday.030: I'll be at every one going *okay, next*. First this, then that, then the river place. I'd run straight through the best part.
hyunjun_ending_someday.031: And I'd have one foot by the door the whole time. Out of habit.
hyunjun_ending_someday.032: We'd be a fast train with someone trying to get off it.
hyunjun_ending_someday.033: I don't want it fast. I want to see every stop.
hyunjun_ending_someday.034: Me too. I really do. I want to be *in* it when it gets here. Not already at the next thing.
hyunjun_ending_someday.035: Neither of you says *wait*. It isn't waiting. It's the difference between running for a train and knowing when it comes.
hyunjun_ending_someday.036: So we give it a stop. A real one. With a time. Then it's not a maybe. It's on the map.
hyunjun_ending_someday.037: December. The date on the record. Last train, twenty-three fifty-one, from here. Second car from the back. Tape or no tape.
hyunjun_ending_someday.039: The pen. You've still got it. We're going to need to add to the map.
hyunjun_ending_someday.040: You check your coat pocket. The front desk's pen is there. Neither of you gave it back. It belongs to the map now.
hyunjun_ending_someday.042: Triangle kimbap. Tuna. *Not* squashed. I'll carry it in a box. I'll carry it like an egg.
hyunjun_ending_someday.043: And I'll ask you something on the bridge. When the windows stop being mirrors. You can probably guess. Don't answer now. I'd like to ask it properly.
hyunjun_ending_someday.044: "December. Twenty-three fifty-one. I'll be on the platform early."
hyunjun_ending_someday.045: I'll be earlier. I'm going to be so early they'll think I work here.
hyunjun_ending_someday.046: "And until December? You're just not going to speak to me?"
hyunjun_ending_someday.047: I'm seeing you Tuesday. There's a new ice cream at the cat store. I intend to see you constantly.
hyunjun_ending_someday.048: It's one stop we're not rushing. Everything else, I'm rushing. Get used to it.
hyunjun_ending_someday.049: The rails start to sing. Far down the tunnel, two white lights, getting bigger.
hyunjun_ending_someday.050: The first train pulls in and opens every door for the two of you and nobody else.
hyunjun_ending_someday.051: You get on. He stays on the yellow line, hands in the pockets of the bomber, both feet flat, not stepping forward.
hyunjun_ending_someday.052: Look at me. I'm all right. We both know the name. We both know the date. Nobody's running after anybody.
hyunjun_ending_someday.055: The doors close between you, the way they did once, at a different station, on the end of a sentence.
hyunjun_ending_someday.056: This time the sentence was finished first.
hyunjun_ending_someday.057: He raises one hand. He holds it for eight counts, and then one more, smiling. Then the platform slides away, and he lets it.
hyunjun_ending_someday.058: The train climbs out of the ground. The bridge. The river, going pink at the edges. The windows show you everything that's out there.
